source_name: OpenSky Network Trino historical query interface
owner: Aviation live aircraft pipeline (Fetcher Agent) — not yet implemented

license.name: Research-restricted / not open by default
license.attribution: OpenSky Network data is accessible to university-affiliated researchers, governmental organisations, aviation authorities, or separately licensed private/commercial entities. Commercial / private entities must contact OpenSky for a licence. Not authorised for use until access is approved and a separate work order is filed.

source_urls.data_access_request: https://opensky-network.org/ → My OpenSky → Request Data Access

what_it_provides: Historical aircraft state vectors via a Trino SQL interface (table: state_vectors_data4). Retention is unlimited. Not a live feed; this is for backfilling aviation_aircraft_observations with historical tracks and enabling timeline playback / research analysis.
fields_collected: Not yet collected — no fetcher or normalizer is implemented in the current code. When the future work order lands, the expected fields will mirror aviation_aircraft_latest / aviation_aircraft_observations (icao24 hex, callsign, origin_country, time_position, last_contact, lon, lat, baro_altitude, on_ground, velocity, true_track, vertical_rate, sensors, etc.).

refresh_policy.schedule_note: No fetcher runs today. When access is approved, refresh cadence will be set by a dedicated work order.

freshness_policy.notes: Historical data has no freshness policy in the usual sense. Backfill runs are expected to be one-shot or rare (e.g. a single 5-year backfill), not recurring.

raw_storage.bucket: needs contract detail — propose god-eyes-raw (same as the rest of the pipeline) and a per-OpenSky source key once the fetcher lands
raw_storage.path_pattern: raw/layer_01_aviation/opensky_trino/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{fetch_run_id}/payload.{ext} (per PROJECT_CONTROL.md §13 raw path pattern; not yet used in code)

normalizer.notes: When implemented, a new normalizer should live in services/normalizer/src/layers/layer_01_aviation/ alongside the other aviation normalizers.

target_tables: aviation_aircraft_observations (write target once fetcher lands; today the row in aviation_aircraft_sources is informational only)

aviation_aircraft_sources (one row already exists: source_id='opensky_trino', layer_id='layer_01_aviation', license_type='research_restricted', is_live=FALSE, is_historical=TRUE, is_active=FALSE — see migration 012)

api_endpoints.notes: No API or WebSocket surface is defined for this source today. Historical backfill would land in aviation_aircraft_observations, which is already exposed indirectly via the latest-aircraft API once writes begin. No new API surface is planned for the backfill itself.

frontend_usage.notes: No frontend changes are planned for the historical backfill itself. Once written, the data would surface through the existing /api/aviation/aircraft/* endpoints, but the frontend does not currently distinguish OpenSky from Airplanes.live data.

tests: tests/data/layer_01_aviation/test_aviation_live_aircraft_migration.py (only verifies the aviation_aircraft_sources DB row exists; no functional fetcher tests)
known_limitations: No fetcher, normalizer, or runtime pipeline is implemented. The DB row in aviation_aircraft_sources is informational only.

Access requires an application at https://opensky-network.org/ and may be declined; eligibility is restricted to university-affiliated researchers, governmental organisations, aviation authorities, or separately licensed private/commercial entities.
OpenSky REST API is not a viable substitute — it is heavily rate-limited for anonymous users and not suitable for the 5s refresh cadence the current build requires (per ADR-002).
Per ADR-002, this source must not block the current build. The decision is 'Implement when access is granted'.
notes: DB source row pre-registered in migration 012_aviation_live_aircraft_tables.sql with is_live=FALSE, is_historical=TRUE, is_active=FALSE, refresh_interval_s=86400.
This file documents the future-only status without pretending it is active. The schema supports a future backfill, but no source code, contract, or migration outside the source row exists today.

Adding a fetcher requires a dedicated work order that covers (a) access approval evidence, (b) a new fetcher module, (c) a new normalizer, (d) any contract changes, and (e) the appropriate 'needs contract detail' resolution before any code is written.
